result.title: LEVI: Benchmarking Visual Identity Fidelity with Verifiable Low-Entropy Constructs
result.summary: Modern generative models can produce visually plausible images while violating exact identity constraints. Evaluating such failures requires distinguishing violations of the requested identity from permissible variation in appearance. We introduce Low-Entropy Visual Identity (LEVI), which characterizes visual identities determined by compact facts and explicit rules. The low-entropy requirement concerns identity uncertainty, while appearance may remain diverse. We formulate identity fidelity in terms of the probability that a conditional image distribution assigns to the identities permitted by the prompt. Visual Identity Spaces (VIS) formalize this distinction by specifying admissible identity values and which different realizations express the same identity. Building on this formulation, we develop Verifiable Visual Grammar (VVG), a declarative language whose typed primitives and compositional constraints describe identity-bearing structures. Using this grammar, we build a benchmark for image generation. It assesses each output against the task's identity requirements, drawing evidence from the final pixels. The curated benchmark contains 1,375 tasks spanning 120 base identity spaces across six domains. Among ten evaluated model configurations, the highest whole-task pass rate is 58.69%. These results reveal a persistent gap between visually plausible images and faithful realization of their specified identities. Project page (forthcoming): https://maxiao0234.github.io/LEVI/.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Low-Entropy Visual Identity（LEVI）框架，用 Visual Identity Spaces 区分「身份事实」与「允许的外观变化」，并设计可验证的声明式语法 VVG，据此构建覆盖 6 个领域、1,375 个任务的图像生成基准，从最终像素检验输出是否满足身份要求；十个模型配置中最高整体通过率仅 58.69%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「身份必要信息 vs 允许变化」的划分与基于像素的规则化验证，可供核查在 latent 视觉表示中如何界定内容保真与无关扰动，以及如何用证据判断视觉信息是否被真正使用；但属图像生成评测，未涉及推理状态，联系仅为概念性。
